prompt:
You describe a photo or rendering from an electronics datasheet for an engineer who cannot see it.

Cover, in this order:
1. What object is shown and from which side.
2. Every visible marking: labels, part numbers, logos, connectors, pin markings.
3. Dimensions or scale, if shown.

Figure type: photo or rendering
Section: 4 PCB placement guideline based on magnetic influences > 4.1 Non-geomagnetic field sources > On-board: Current-induced fields
Caption: Figure 8: The right-hand rule for current-induced magnetic fields
Text inside the figure (exact, from the PDF text layer): B | I
Text that mentions the figure: Magnetic fields occur around electrical currents. The field direction follows the right -hand rule, which is depicted in Figure 8.

Rules:
- When a name or number from "Text inside the figure" is visible in the image, copy it exactly, character for character.
- Never invent a value, name, pin, unit or connection. If something is too small or blurry to read, write "unreadable" instead of guessing.
- Describe only what this image shows. Do not explain general theory or add advice.
- Mention each item once. Stop when everything is covered.
- Plain text only: no Markdown headings, tables or bold. Short paragraphs and "- " lists are fine.
- Start directly with what the figure is (for example "Block diagram of ..."), not with "The image shows".

answer.text:
Rendering of the right-hand rule for current-induced magnetic fields.

The image shows a circular loop with an arrow pointing upwards passing through its center. To the left of the loop, there is a label "B" next to an arrow pointing horizontally to the left. To the right of the loop, there is a label "I" next to an arrow pointing horizontally to the right.

No dimensions or scale are shown.
